audit.whatIsWrong: content.wants.you[1] says 'Wither him the moment he flashes Unstoppable Force so the unstoppable engage fizzles into a free trade', and content.mid says 'hold Wither so the second he ults in you slow the engage to nothing'. Both tell the player Wither answers the ult itself.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is unstoppable — a slow applied as he casts does not reduce the dash, the travel or the knockup. The advice is not merely imprecise, it is the wrong mental model: a Nasus expecting the engage to 'fizzle' will stand still and eat the full knockup. What Wither actually does is delete everything AFTER he lands, which is where all of Malphite's follow-up damage lives. Same button, opposite timing logic.
audit.corrected: You cannot slow the dash. Cast Wither the instant he lands — his follow-up is where the damage is, and that is what Wither takes away.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json R description and dash flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam is never mentioned in either layer. Not once.
audit.why: Ground Slam is on a flat 7s cooldown at every rank, deals magic damage scaling with Malphite's OWN armour, and reduces the attack speed of everyone it hits. Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack and Soul Eater is life steal on basic attacks — so Malphite's E cuts Nasus's damage AND his sustain with one button, every seven seconds. It is the single most anti-Nasus ability in Malphite's kit and the file does not know it exists. It also means his armour purchases are offensive purchases, which changes how you read his build.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam (E): flat 7s, damage scales off his armour, and it cuts your attack speed — which is your Q damage and your lifesteal. Step up when it is spent.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json Q autoReset and P Soul Eater

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield is never named. content.early instead says 'his Soul Eater equivalent doesn't exist, so your lifesteal eats the poke', which is close to the opposite of the truth.
audit.why: Granite Shield absorbs damage up to 10% of Malphite's maximum health and RECHARGES whenever he has not been hit for a few seconds. That is his early sustain, and it is specifically a buffer against exactly the thing Nasus wants to do — land one big empowered Siphoning Strike. Chipping the shield off with a normal auto or Spirit Fire before committing the stacked Q is the concrete sequencing rule this matchup has been missing.
audit.corrected: Granite Shield eats 10% of his max health and recharges out of combat — break it with a throwaway auto before you spend a stacked Q into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. breakdown.cooldowns names only Unstoppable Force and then says 'Saved for fights. Lane is fine without it' — which explicitly tells the player there is no lane cooldown worth tracking.
audit.why: There are two, both better than his ultimate for lane purposes: Ground Slam at a flat 7s, and Granite Shield's out-of-combat recharge. Seismic Shard is also 8s flat and costs 70/75/80/85/90 mana, so an early Malphite genuinely cannot spam it. Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100 against Nasus's own 120/100/80, so Nasus's ultimate is up more often than his at every rank.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam flat 7s; Granite Shield recharges out of combat; Seismic Shard 8s at 70-90 mana; Unstoppable Force 130/115/100 against your 120/100/80.

audit.whatIsWrong: Malphite's W is repeatedly called a passive that stacks armour — 'his armor and W passive', 'W armor-stack', 'Stack armor and W passive' in content.whys[3], whys[5], spikes[2].text and wants.foe[2].
audit.why: Thunderclap is an activated ability with an attack-attack reset, not a passive. The durability the file is trying to describe is Granite Shield, which is the actual passive and does have a concrete number attached to it. I have re-pointed those four strings at Granite Shield rather than assert anything about W's armour, which I could not confirm from Riot's description text.
audit.corrected: The recurring absorb is Granite Shield (P), 10% max health, recharging out of combat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard is described as a chip-and-slow ('just chips and slows', 'slow you off CS').
audit.why: It steals Move Speed for 3 seconds — he gains what you lose. In a lane where Nasus's only escape is walking, a two-way swing is materially different from a one-way slow, and it is why his Q into a jungle gank is so much stronger than the file implies.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard steals your move speed — he speeds up by exactly what you lose.

audit.why: 53.85% over 1196 games, and the chart (Nasus early, Malphite around 6 and first item, Nasus late) is a sensible shape for it. No chart edit needed here.

edits.before: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — Saved for fights. Lane is fine without it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Ground Slam: flat 7s and it cuts your attack speed — step up when spent. - Granite Shield: 10% max HP, recharges out of combat.

edits.before: Malphite at levels 1-2 has zero kill pressure on you — his Seismic Shard (Q) just chips and slows, and his Soul Eater equivalent doesn't exist, so your lifesteal eats the poke. Stand in the wave and stack Siphoning Strike off every minion; he literally cannot stop you from farming. The one thing to mind is his Q slow setting up a jungle gank, so ward the river and don't overextend past the lane brush while he's pushing.
edits.after: Malphite at levels 1-2 has zero kill pressure on you — Seismic Shard (Q) chips and steals your move speed, and at 70+ mana a cast he cannot spam it. Stand in the wave and stack Siphoning Strike off every minion. Two things to mind: Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health and recharges whenever he goes untouched, so chip it off before any real trade, and his Q slow sets up ganks — ward the river.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a quiet farming stalemate — neither of you wins an extended trade yet, so keep hoarding stacks while his armor and W passive let him shrug your early Q. Then at 6 respect Unstoppable Force: it's his ONLY real engage, an unstoppable point-and-click knockup, and into a gank it can kill you. Don't shove into his tower with your jungler unknown; hold Wither so the second he ults in you slow the engage to nothing and walk away even.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a quiet farming stalemate, but Ground Slam (E) is the tool that actually hurts you: a flat 7s cooldown that cuts your attack speed, and Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack. Time your step-ups off it. At 6 respect Unstoppable Force — it is unstoppable, so Wither cannot slow the dash; cast Wither the instant he lands instead and his follow-up is nothing. Do not shove into his tower with his jungler unknown.

edits.before: Pure farming standoff: his early armor and W passive let him eat your low-stack Q, so it comes down to who plays the wave cleaner.
edits.after: Pure farming standoff: Granite Shield and his early armour eat your low-stack Q, so it comes down to who plays the wave cleaner.

edits.after: His first armour item plus a recharged Granite Shield survives your empowered Q burst — his durability briefly outpaces your stack count.

edits.after: Malphite's first armour item plus Granite Shield's 10% max-health absorb eats your early Q autos — the one stretch his durability outpaces your stacks.

edits.after: Wither him the instant Unstoppable Force lands — you can't slow the dash, but you can kill the follow-up

notes: The packet's one suspectName ('Land Unstoppable Force' in wants.foe[1]) is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name, leading verb. The flagged 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice' defect was real and its cause was that breakdown.cooldowns actively told the player there was nothing to track in lane. Ground Slam being absent from the entire matchup is the biggest miss: a flat 7s attack-speed cut is a direct tax on Siphoning Strike and Soul Eater, i.e. on both halves of Nasus's kit. One item I deliberately did NOT assert: several strings claim Malphite's W stacks armour. Riot's Thunderclap description in the kit mentions only the sonic boom and aftershocks — the derived flags list a shield but no armour — so rather than confirm or deny it I re-pointed those strings at Granite Shield, which is measurable. If someone can verify Thunderclap's armour component on the wiki, those four strings could be sharpened further.
